title: Europe now takes your fingerprints at the border
snippet: The EU Entry/Exit System replaced passport stamps for UK and other non-EU travellers. It's been fully live since April 2026.
bullets: EES launched on 12 October 2025 and became fully operational on 10 April 2026.[1]
UK passport holders give fingerprints and a photo on their first visit. It's free.[2]
It applies to non-EU nationals on short stays. Ireland and Cyprus aren't covered.[1][2]

report.t: EES records entries and exits digitally instead of stamping passports.[1]
Expect fingerprints and a face photo on your first entry, and possibly a longer wait.[2]
EES is for non-EU nationals.[1] If you hold an EU passport, you're outside it, so carry the right one.

Arrive with extra time on your first post-EES trip, since registration can take longer.[2] EES applies to non-EU nationals.[1] If you're also an EU citizen, show your EU passport in Schengen. Through Dover, Folkestone or St Pancras, checks happen before you leave the UK.[2]

why: If you have an EU passport, using it in Schengen keeps you out of EES entirely.
tryit: Before your next EU trip, decide which passport you'll use and keep it with your boarding pass.
qa: What is EES?
The EU's digital Entry/Exit System, which registers non-EU travellers with fingerprints and a photo.[1]
When did it start?
12 October 2025, fully operational from 10 April 2026.[1]
Do I pay for EES?
No, registration is free.[2]
Does it apply to Ireland or Cyprus?
Do EU citizens need it?
No. It applies to non-EU nationals.[1]

title: The UK scrapped non-dom status. Here's the new 4-year rule
snippet: Since 6 April 2025, UK tax depends on residence, not domicile. New arrivals can get a 4-year break on foreign income.
bullets: The remittance basis ended on 6 April 2025.[1]
Qualifying new residents (after 10 years abroad) can claim relief on foreign income and gains for 4 years.[1]
Claiming means losing your tax-free personal allowance and CGT allowance.[1]

report.h: Domicile is out, residence is in
report.t: UK tax now hinges on tax residence under the Statutory Residence Test, not domicile.[2]
If you become UK resident after 10 years of non-residence, you can claim relief on eligible foreign income and gains for up to 4 tax years.[1]
Claiming costs your personal allowance and CGT annual exemption, and you claim on your Self Assessment return.[1]

report.h: Questions to ask a tax adviser
report.t: Am I UK tax resident under the Statutory Residence Test? Do I qualify for the 4-year FIG regime? Is claiming worth losing my personal allowance?[1] Residence-based rules replaced domicile from 6 April 2025,[2] so old non-dom advice may be out of date.

why: With several nationalities, your UK tax depends on where you're resident, not which passports you hold.
tryit: If you have income abroad (Brazil, EU), book one session with a cross-border tax adviser.
qa: What replaced non-dom?
A residence-based system, with a 4-year FIG regime for qualifying new residents, from 6 April 2025.[1]
Who qualifies?
UK tax residents in their first 4 years after at least 10 years of non-UK residence.[1]
What's the catch?
You lose tax-free allowances for Income Tax and CGT when you claim.[1]
How do I claim?
On your Self Assessment tax return.[1]
Is this tax advice?
No. It's general gov.uk information.

sources.title: Check if you can claim the 4-year foreign income and gains regime - GOV.UK

title: Brazilian and British? Both countries are fine with that
snippet: The UK allows dual citizenship, and since October 2023 Brazil places no restriction on dual nationality.
bullets: Dual citizenship is allowed in the UK, and you don't need to apply for it.[1]
Since October 2023, Brazil doesn't restrict dual nationality.[2]
Since May 2016, Brazil doesn't make naturalised citizens give up their old nationality.[2]

report.t: You can be a British citizen and a citizen of other countries, with no application needed.[1]
Brazil removed restrictions on dual nationality in October 2023.[2]
More passports can mean more options, like entering Schengen on an EU passport, which keeps you outside EES.[3]

Keep all passports valid; renewals can take months. Use the right passport at each border. In Schengen, an EU passport keeps you outside EES.[3] The UK doesn't require you to apply for dual citizenship,[1] and Brazil has no restriction since October 2023.[2]

why: Your multiple nationalities are an asset. Know the rules and use them.
tryit: Check the expiry dates on all your passports today and set renewal reminders 9 months ahead.
qa: Does the UK allow dual citizenship?
Yes, and you don't need to apply for it.[1]
Can Brazilians hold another nationality?
Yes. Since October 2023 Brazil imposes no restriction on dual nationality.[2]
Can Brazil take away my citizenship?
Only in narrow cases for naturalised citizens, such as fraud.[2]
Which passport should I use in Europe?
EES applies to non-EU nationals, so an EU passport keeps you outside it.[3]

title: Your accent isn't the problem. Clarity is
snippet: In a classic study, how strong an accent was didn't slow listeners down. Hard-to-understand speech did.
bullets: Munro & Derwing (1995): 20 native listeners judged true/false sentences from native and accented speakers.[1]
Speech rated hard to understand took longer to process.[1]
But the strength of the accent wasn't linked to processing time.[1]

report.t: Listeners weren't slowed down by how strong the accent was.[1]
What slowed listeners was speech rated hard to understand.[1]
Work on the sounds and stress that cause misunderstandings, not on erasing where you're from.

Focus on what blocks understanding: word stress (PHOtograph vs phoTOgraphy), clear vowel length, and pausing between ideas. The study found accent strength itself didn't slow listeners; low comprehensibility did.[1] Record yourself and ask: would a busy listener catch every word?

why: Your Brazilian accent is part of you. Clarity is what changes how you're heard.
tryit: Record a 30-second voice note, play it back, and mark one word a listener could mishear. Practise just that word.
qa: Does a foreign accent make me harder to understand?
Not by itself. Accent strength wasn't related to processing time; comprehensibility was.[1]
What should I focus on?
Being easy to understand: the sounds and stress patterns that cause misunderstandings.[1]
Who did this study?
Murray Munro and Tracey Derwing, in Language and Speech, 1995.[1]
Was it Portuguese speakers?
No. The accented speakers were native Mandarin speakers.[1]

title: Shadowing: repeat native speech a split second behind
snippet: Speech shadowing, repeating what you hear with a tiny delay, is a lab technique that's also used for language learning.
bullets: Speech shadowing means repeating speech with a short delay after you hear it.[1]
The delay reflects how long the brain takes to process and respond.[1]
It's used in language learning, interpreting and singing.[1]

report.t: Play audio and speak along a beat behind, copying the rhythm and melody.[1]
It trains listening and speaking at once, which is why it's used in language learning and interpreting.[1]
No textbook needed. Just a podcast you love and 5 minutes.

1. Listen to a 30-second clip once. 2. Play it again and speak along a beat behind. 3. Repeat three times, then record yourself. Shadowing is a recognised technique in language learning and interpreting.[1] Pick speakers whose style you'd like to sound like.

why: It builds the music of English, its rhythm and stress, which shapes how natural you sound.
tryit: Pick a 1-minute clip from a podcast you like and shadow it 3 times today.
qa: What is shadowing?
Repeating speech with a short delay after hearing it.[1]
Is it used for language learning?
Yes, along with interpreting and singing.[1]
How long should I practise?
Start with 5 minutes a day so it's easy to stick with.
What should I shadow?
Clear speech you enjoy, like a favourite podcast host.

title: Learn words right before you forget them
snippet: Spaced repetition brings words back at growing intervals. It's ideal for vocabulary.
bullets: Spaced repetition schedules reviews at growing intervals to beat the forgetting curve.[1]
It's especially well suited to learning vocabulary.[1]

report.t: Review just as a memory starts to fade, and each review lasts longer.[1]
It shines when you need to learn lots of items and keep them for good.[1]

report.h: Let the app do the timing
report.t: Apps like Anki schedule your reviews automatically.[1]

Put the phrase in a real sentence, add the audio if you can, and keep each card to one idea. Spaced repetition is especially well suited to vocabulary.[1] Apps like Anki schedule reviews just as you're about to forget.[1] Five minutes a day is plenty.

why: Phrasal verbs and idioms stick when an app brings them back at the right moment.
tryit: Add 5 English phrases you heard this week to a spaced-repetition app.
qa: What is spaced repetition?
Reviewing material at increasing intervals to beat the forgetting curve.[1]
Is it good for vocabulary?
Yes, it's well suited to vocabulary.[1]
Which app?
Anki is a popular option and uses the FSRS scheduler.[1]
How many words a day?
Start small, 5 to 10 new items, so reviews stay manageable.
